name: Texaf Bilembo
funding: Texaf, listed on Euronext Brussels, is founder and head sponsor of the centre. Its income is 85% Kinshasa real estate, 12% a sandstone quarry and 3% digital.
watch: Texaf is 62.9% held by Société Financière Africaine and 10% by the Cha family. Bilembo covers over 1,000 m² of exhibition and workshop space.
records_note: Posts a 2025 activity report and an undated partner logo strip; no accounts or board named, though founder Texaf publishes its own audited accounts.

name: Thapong Visual Arts Centre
funding: Board-run centre funded by the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Culture (P2.2M for the 2014 refit). Partners: HB Botswana (2024), BTC Foundation (2018), DTC Botswana and FNB Foundation (2014).
watch: De Beers gave P75,000 toward the 2014 refit. That is twelve years old and not a current funding line.
records_note: No website of its own was found; news items name partners and a 2014 board chair, but no reports, accounts or current board are public.

name: The Bowes Museum
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England, Durham County Council, National Lottery Heritage Fund £250k, Wolfson Foundation, Swire Charitable Trust, Art Fund, about 20 other trusts; Darlington Building Society, Global Radio.
watch: Arms and Armour Heritage Trust is a heritage charity, not an arms maker. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual report on its site; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register, a supporters page names donors, trustees are listed.

name: The Factory Contemporary Arts Centre
funding: Founded 2016; self-funded social enterprise where art sales and an on-site cafe pay for programmes.
records_note: The live site returns an empty page; archived copies show no reports, accounts, donor list or board, only a founder and former curatorial staff.

name: The MAC
funding: £3.0M income (FY2025). Arts Council NI £1.1M, Belfast City Council £120k, Freelands Foundation £126k, Art Fund, Henry Moore Foundation, Dormant Accounts; sponsors include Clever Fulton Rankin.
watch: Regulated by the Charity Commission for Northern Ireland.
records_note: The NI register holds annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; the supporters page shows tiered logos without names, and trustees are listed.

name: The Model
watch: Regional contemporary arts center in Sligo.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2024 audited accounts and a 15-member board with company secretary, and a footer funder-logo image with no names or date.

name: The Muse Multi Studios
funding: Won Culture Resource's Abbara Program grant (round 7, 2022). The Australian Government and Creative Australia support its Qubit fellowship (2026). The Spanish Embassy is a named partner.
watch: Opened Muse Gallery in Khartoum in 2022; since the April 2023 war it works between Sudan and Egypt and runs the Sudan Art Archive.
records_note: Posts narrative year reviews for 2023 to 2025 with no figures; no accounts, no standing funder list, and only its five staff are named.

name: The Renaissance Society
funding: Mellon, Teiger and Warhol foundations; Edlis Neeson, Pritzker Traubert and Zell family foundations for the Next Century Fund; Illinois Arts Council; University of Chicago, about 5 percent. FY2025 expenses $1.9M.
watch: University-based non-collecting kunsthalle; non-corporate academic funding.
records_note: Annual reports 2019-20 to 2024-25 on its site, Form 990s on ProPublica, an undated sponsors list naming funders, and 25 board members listed.

name: The Showroom
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio Organisation (NPO), Paul Hamlyn Foundation, Esmée Fairbairn Foundation. Registered Charity No. 1055262.
watch: Known for its 'Communal Knowledge' program, linking international artists with local housing estates and immigrant communities.

name: Tirana Art Lab
funding: Independent non-profit founded 2010 by Adela Demetja. Named supporters: Creative Europe, Allianz Kulturstiftung, Pro Helvetia, Robert Bosch Foundation, European Cultural Foundation, Albania's Ministry of Culture, Municipality of Tirana.
watch: No permanent venue from 2018; works with local partners. Runs the Curating with Care programme and the Beyond Matter EU project (2019 to 2023).
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, board or standing funder page; supporters are credited only on individual project pages.

name: Towner Eastbourne
funding: £3.6M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £538k, Eastbourne Borough Council £414k (2024), Newhaven Enterprise Zone, Rick Mather David Sieff Foundation, Fidelity Foundation, Art Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund.
records_note: Annual reviews 2020-21 to 2024-25 are on its blog; accounts are on the Charity Commission register; funders show as logos; the board is listed.
